question: In the treatment of iridocyclitis, systemic corticosteroids or immunosuppressive agents (such as methotrexate or azathioprine) are used as first-line therapy before attempting topical steroids and cycloplegics.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is FALSE. The correct ladder is: (1) Topical steroids + cycloplegics → (2) Periocular or systemic steroids if needed → (3) Steroid-sparing immunosuppressants for chronic/refractory disease. Jumping straight to systemic agents is incorrect and exposes patients to unnecessary side effects.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is FALSE. The therapeutic ladder for iridocyclitis starts with LOCAL therapy: topical corticosteroids (prednisolone acetate drops) and cycloplegics. Systemic steroids are added only if topical therapy is inadequate or if there is severe posterior involvement. Steroid-sparing immunosuppressants (methotrexate, azathioprine, mycophenolate) are reserved for chronic/recurrent disease requiring systemic steroids for >3 months.
